The ''[[James Bond]]'' video game franchise is a series centering on [[Ian Fleming]]'s fictional [[James Bond (literary character)|British MI6 agent of the same name]]. Games of the series have been predominantly [[shooter game]]s, with some games of other genres including [[role-playing video games|role-playing]] and [[adventure games]]. Several games are based upon the [[Production of the James Bond films|''James Bond'' films]] and developed and published by a variety of companies. The intellectual property is owned by [[Danjaq]].

===Early era (1983–1994)===
The first [[James Bond]] game, ''[[Shaken but Not Stirred]]'', was released in 1982.<ref>{{Cite web|url = https://www.gamespew.com/2021/10/the-best-james-bond-games/2/|title = The Best James Bond Games|date = 5 October 2021|access-date = 25 October 2021|archive-date = 25 October 2021|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20211025170255/https://www.gamespew.com/2021/10/the-best-james-bond-games/2/|url-status = live}}</ref> In 1984, [[Parker Brothers]] published [[James Bond 007 (1984 video game)|''James Bond 007'']] for multiple platforms.<ref>{{cite magazine|magazine=The Video Game Update includes Computer Entertainer|volume=3|issue=2|date=May 1984|title=Atari 2600|ISSN=0890-2143|ref={{sfnref|The Video Game Update includes Computer Entertainer|1984a|}}|url=https://archive.gamehistory.org/item/f316eb98-2116-4984-9360-1263e60e0acd|accessdate=June 10, 2026|via=Video Game History Foundation}}</ref>

Since 1983, there have been numerous video games based on the films, [[Ian Fleming]]'s novels, and original scripts created by the [[video game developer|developer]] or [[video game publisher|publisher]] of the game. [[Mindscape (company)|Mindscape]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.mi6-hq.com/sections/articles/legacy_goldfinger.php3|title=Goldfinger – The Legacy|website=MI6-HQ|access-date=25 October 2021|archive-date=25 October 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211025211457/https://www.mi6-hq.com/sections/articles/legacy_goldfinger.php3|url-status=live}}</ref> [[Domark]],<ref>{{Cite web|url = https://www.mi6-hq.com/sections/games/tld|title = The Living Daylights (1987)|date = January 2016|access-date = 25 October 2021|archive-date = 25 October 2021|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20211025211721/https://www.mi6-hq.com/sections/games/tld|url-status = live}}</ref> [[Interplay Entertainment|Interplay]],<ref>{{Cite web|url = https://www.pcgamer.com/uk/saturday-crapshoot-james-bond-the-stealth-affair-aka-operation-stealth/|title = Crapshoot: The James Bond game starring 'John Glames'|website = [[PC Gamer]]|date = 21 August 2021|last1 = Cobbett|first1 = Richard|access-date = 25 October 2021|archive-date = 25 October 2021|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20211025212323/https://www.pcgamer.com/uk/saturday-crapshoot-james-bond-the-stealth-affair-aka-operation-stealth/|url-status = live}}</ref> and [[THQ]]<ref>{{Cite web |url = https://www.mi6-hq.com/sections/games/jbj|title = James Bond Jr. (1992)| website=MI6-HQ |date = January 2016|access-date = 25 October 2021|archive-date = 25 October 2021|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20211025212545/https://www.mi6-hq.com/sections/games/jbj|url-status = live}}</ref> all created James Bond games.

The video games were somewhat profitable{{Citation needed|date=October 2020}} in the 1980s and early 1990s, featuring a mixture of styles including [[side-scroller|side-scrolling]] action and [[text adventure]].

===Nintendo era (1995–1998)===
The popularity of the James Bond video game series did not rise quickly until 1997's ''[[GoldenEye 007 (1997 video game)|GoldenEye 007]]'' by [[Rare (company)|Rare]] for the [[Nintendo 64]]. ''GoldenEye 007'' expanded on the plot of the film ''[[GoldenEye]]'' and is a [[first-person shooter]] with a [[multiplayer]] mode.<ref>{{Cite web|url = https://www.gamespew.com/2021/10/the-best-james-bond-games/11/|title = The Best James Bond Games|date = 5 October 2021|access-date = 25 October 2021|archive-date = 25 October 2021|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20211025171506/https://www.gamespew.com/2021/10/the-best-james-bond-games/11/|url-status = live}}</ref> The game received very positive reviews<ref name="gamerankings">{{cite web|title=GoldenEye 007 Reviews|publisher=gamerankings.com|url=http://www.gamerankings.com/n64/197462-goldeneye-007/index.html|access-date=29 January 2006|archive-date=2 June 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160602171113/http://www.gamerankings.com/n64/197462-goldeneye-007/index.html|url-status=live}}</ref> and sold over eight million copies.<ref name="8million">{{cite web| date=24 September 2002| url=https://news.microsoft.com/2002/09/24/microsoft-acquires-video-game-powerhouse-rare-ltd/| title=Microsoft Acquires Video Game Powerhouse Rare Ltd.| publisher=Microsoft| access-date=13 May 2006| archive-date=21 February 2016| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160221113108/http://news.microsoft.com/2002/09/24/microsoft-acquires-video-game-powerhouse-rare-ltd/| url-status=live}}</ref>

In 1998, [[Nintendo]] released ''[[James Bond 007 (1998 video game)|James Bond 007]]'' for the [[Game Boy]] developed by [[Saffire (company)|Saffire]]. The game features a story including characters from multiple James Bond films, such as [[Oddjob]] and [[Jaws (James Bond)|Jaws]]. It also incorporates gambling [[minigame]]s, such as [[Baccarat]] and [[Blackjack]].

===Electronic Arts era (1999–2005)===
[[Electronic Arts]] (EA) took over the license from MGM Interactive when a video game based on ''[[Tomorrow Never Dies]]'' was in development in 1998. Taking the initial concepts for the [[Tomorrow Never Dies (video game)|video game adaptation]], developer [[Black Ops Entertainment]] handled the final form of the title and the game saw the light of day in 1999 on [[PlayStation (console)|PlayStation]]<ref>{{Cite web|url = https://www.gamespew.com/2021/10/the-best-james-bond-games/3/|title = The Best James Bond Games|date = 5 October 2021|access-date = 25 October 2021|archive-date = 25 October 2021|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20211025170532/https://www.gamespew.com/2021/10/the-best-james-bond-games/3/|url-status = live}}</ref> and met mixed reviews from critics, albeit becoming a financial success. The following entry was to be based on ''[[The World Is Not Enough]]'', consisting of several versions released on multiple platforms, including one on [[The World Is Not Enough (Nintendo 64 video game)|Nintendo 64]] developed by [[Eurocom]],<ref name="15 Best James Bond 007 Games Ever">{{Cite web|url=https://www.denofgeek.com/games/best-james-bond-007-games-ever/|title=15 Best James Bond 007 Games Ever|date=30 September 2021|access-date=25 October 2021|archive-date=25 October 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211025213714/https://www.denofgeek.com/games/best-james-bond-007-games-ever/|url-status=live}}</ref> a version for [[The World Is Not Enough (PlayStation video game)|PlayStation]] developed by Black Ops Entertainment, and [[The World Is Not Enough (2001 video game)|Game Boy Color]] by 2n Productions, with all three meeting different results in spite of being commercially successful. Unlike the former two versions – first-person shooters – the Game Boy Color version is played from a top-down perspective.<ref name=ALL>{{cite web |url=http://www.allgame.com/game.php?id=31053&tab=review |title=The World Is Not Enough (GBC) – Review |last=Thompson |first=Jon |publisher=AllGame |access-date=2014-12-07 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141207170159/http://www.allgame.com/game.php?id=31053&tab=review |archive-date=2014-12-07}}</ref>

In 2001, EA released ''[[James Bond 007: Agent Under Fire|Agent Under Fire]]'' for [[PlayStation 2]], [[GameCube]], and [[Xbox (console)|Xbox]], featuring an original storyline<ref>{{Cite web|url = https://www.gamespew.com/2021/10/the-best-james-bond-games/6/|title = The Best James Bond Games|date = 5 October 2021|access-date = 25 October 2021|archive-date = 25 October 2021|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20211025170846/https://www.gamespew.com/2021/10/the-best-james-bond-games/6/|url-status = live}}</ref> and lacking the likeness of then Bond actor [[Pierce Brosnan]].<ref name="15 Best James Bond 007 Games Ever"/> The game added the elements of "rail" shooting and driving segments to a first-person shooter. The game sold nearly 5 million copies, making it the second-most successful game in the series, while only receiving mixed reviews. There are no differences between the console versions.

In 2002, ''[[James Bond 007: Nightfire|Nightfire]]'' was released, coinciding with the 40th anniversary of the film franchise and using Brosnan's likeness for the Bond character, but not his voice.<ref name="15 Best James Bond 007 Games Ever"/> It was developed by [[Eurocom]] for the GameCube, PlayStation 2, and Xbox consoles, with a [[Personal computer game|PC]] port by [[Gearbox Software]] and a [[Mac OS X|Mac]] port by [[Aspyr]]. The computer versions are substantially different from the console versions, featuring different missions, a modified story line, and online play. In 2003, the game also had a [[Game Boy Advance]] version by [[JV Games]], which also differs from both the console versions and PC versions.

In 2004, EA released ''[[James Bond 007: Everything or Nothing|Everything or Nothing]]'', developed by EA Redwood, for the GameCube, PlayStation 2 and Xbox. Unlike the two previous installments, ''Everything or Nothing'' is a [[third-person shooter]] with driving missions, and it stars the voices and likenesses of [[Pierce Brosnan]], [[Judi Dench]], [[Willem Dafoe]] and [[John Cleese]],<ref>{{Cite web|url = https://www.gamespew.com/2021/10/the-best-james-bond-games/8/|title = The Best James Bond Games|date = 5 October 2021|access-date = 25 October 2021|archive-date = 25 October 2021|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20211025171135/https://www.gamespew.com/2021/10/the-best-james-bond-games/8/|url-status = live}}</ref> among others. It was written by the scriptwriter of ''GoldenEye'' and ''Tomorrow Never Dies'', screenwriter [[Bruce Feirstein]], with a plot connected to the [[Roger Moore]] Bond film ''[[A View to a Kill]]''. It was released to mostly positive reviews. A different version of ''[[James Bond 007: Everything or Nothing (GBA video game)|Everything or Nothing]]'' was also developed by [[Griptonite Games]] for the [[Game Boy Advance]].

Later that year, ''[[GoldenEye: Rogue Agent]]'' was released on the same platforms with the exception of the Game Boy Advance version. A first-person shooter loosely connected to the Bond franchise a spin-off, it stars a former MI6 spy<ref name="15 Best James Bond 007 Games Ever"/> known as "GoldenEye", who works for [[Auric Goldfinger]] against [[Julius No|Dr. Julius No]]. The game received mixed reviews. The game was released on PlayStation 2, Xbox, GameCube and Nintendo DS. EA listed ''007 Racing'' and ''GoldenEye: Rogue Agent'' as spin-offs, out of their canonical order they have built.

2005 saw the release of ''[[From Russia with Love (video game)|From Russia with Love]]'', based on the 1963 [[From Russia with Love (film)|film of the same name]]. It stars [[Sean Connery]] as James Bond, and the other characters had the same likeness of the original cast. The game is a third-person shooter in the same style as ''Everything or Nothing'', with expansions in the story and certain details changed (such as trading [[SPECTRE]] for OCTOPUS, due to [[Thunderball (novel)#Controversy|legal problems]]).<ref name="15 Best James Bond 007 Games Ever"/> The game received positive reviews, and was released on GameCube, Xbox, PS2 and PSP.

Electronic Arts announced in 2006 a game based on then-upcoming ''[[Casino Royale (2006 film)|Casino Royale]]'',<ref name="EA CR">{{cite web|url=http://www.mi6-hq.com/sections/articles/gaming_cr_leaked.php3?t=&s=cr&id=01072|title=EA Confirm Casino Royale|website=MI6-HQ.COM|access-date=20 July 2011|archive-date=1 August 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120801160928/http://www.mi6-hq.com/sections/articles/gaming_cr_leaked.php3?t=&s=cr&id=01072|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="LostGame">{{cite web |url=http://www.mi6-hq.com/sections/articles/gaming_ea_casino_royale_lost.php3|title=EA's Lost 007 'Casino Royale' Videogame|website=MI6-HQ|access-date=20 July 2011|archive-date=1 August 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120801161042/http://www.mi6-hq.com/sections/articles/gaming_ea_casino_royale_lost.php3|url-status=live}}</ref> but it ended up being cancelled, because it would not be ready by the film's release in November. This fact, which would lead [[Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer|MGM]] to lose millions in licensing fees, along with EA's commitment to move away from movie franchise games and focus more on internal intellectual properties, led the company to abandon the Bond franchise in May 2006.<ref name="Fritz">{{cite news | url=https://variety.com/2006/digital/features/action-traction-1200506308/ | title=Bond, Superman games on the move | access-date=18 May 2006 | work=Variety | first=Ben | last=Fritz | date=3 May 2006 | archive-date=20 November 2010 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101120222547/http://www.variety.com/article/VR1117942524?categoryid=18&cs=1 | url-status=live }}</ref>

===Activision era (2006–2013)===
Shortly after Electronic Arts abandoned the license, in May 2006, [[Activision]] acquired non-exclusive rights to develop and publish James Bond games, which were to become exclusive in 2007.<ref>{{cite web| url=http://www.shacknews.com/article/41980/activision-acquires-bond-video-game| title=Activision Acquires Bond Video Game License| date=3 May 2006| access-date=3 May 2006| archive-date=27 May 2012| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120527122531/http://www.shacknews.com/article/41980/activision-acquires-bond-video-game| url-status=live}}</ref> Activision's first game was ''[[007: Quantum of Solace|Quantum of Solace]]'', which was based on the 2008 [[Quantum of Solace|film of the same name]] as well as the previous film ''Casino Royale''.<ref>{{Cite web|url = https://www.cbr.com/james-bond-quantum-solace-game-casino-royale/|title = Why the Quantum of Solace Game Was a Casino Royale Game in Disguise|date = October 2021|access-date = 26 October 2021|archive-date = 26 October 2021|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20211026121142/https://www.cbr.com/james-bond-quantum-solace-game-casino-royale/|url-status = live}}</ref> It was developed by [[Treyarch]] for [[PlayStation 3]], [[Xbox 360]], [[Wii]] and PC; [[Eurocom]] for PlayStation 2 and [[Vicarious Visions]] for the Nintendo DS. The game was released on 31 October 2008 and received mixed reviews, with the PlayStation 2 version receiving the best reviews.<ref>{{cite web| url=https://www.metacritic.com/search/all/quantum+of+solace/results| title=Quantum of Solace reviews – Metacritic| website=[[Metacritic]]| access-date=30 January 2014| archive-date=7 April 2016| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160407232402/http://www.metacritic.com/search/all/quantum+of+solace/results| url-status=live}}</ref>

At [[E3 2010]], [[Nintendo]] revealed ''[[GoldenEye 007 (2010 video game)|GoldenEye 007]]'', a remake of the 1997 game that was released on Nintendo 64.  The remake initially targeted and was released for the Wii and Nintendo DS with a more modernized plot based on a script by [[Bruce Feirstein]], with then-Bond actor [[Daniel Craig]] portraying 007.<ref>{{cite web| title=GoldenEye 007 – Hands On Preview| url=http://www.totalvideogames.com/GoldenEye-007/preview-15701.html| last=Earwaker| first=Kiran| publisher=TVG Media Ltd.| date=8 October 2010| access-date=10 November 2010| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101206214349/http://www.totalvideogames.com/GoldenEye-007/preview-15701.html| archive-date=6 December 2010| df=dmy-all}}</ref>  The Wii version was developed by [[Eurocom]] and ran on EngineX, a [[game engine]] previously used for the rail shooter ''[[Dead Space: Extraction]]'', while the Nintendo DS version was developed by [[n-Space]]. It was released in November 2010 in all regions to positive reviews from critics.  Approximately a year later, an enhanced port of the game entitled ''GoldenEye 007: Reloaded'' was released for PlayStation 3 and Xbox 360. The port featured HD graphics, new missions and [[PlayStation Move]] support on the PS3 version.

Activision's third Bond game, ''[[James Bond 007: Blood Stone|Blood Stone]]'' was released on the same day as ''GoldenEye 007'' in November 2010. Developed by [[Bizarre Creations]], the game returned to being a third person shooter, featured an original story and starred Daniel Craig, Judi Dench<ref name="15 Best James Bond 007 Games Ever"/> and [[Joss Stone]], the latter of which also sang on the game's theme song "I'll Take It All".<ref>{{Cite news|url = https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/newsbeat-10666483|title = Joss Stone to play virtual Bond Girl in 007:Blood Stone|work = BBC News|date = 16 July 2010|access-date = 26 October 2021|archive-date = 26 October 2021|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20211026121450/https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/newsbeat-10666483|url-status = live}}</ref> It was released for PlayStation 3, Xbox 360, PC and DS and received mixed reviews from critics. Developer Bizarre Creations was closed down by Activision in early 2011 just a few months after the game's release.

On 19 April 2012, [[Activision]] announced plans for a game titled ''[[007 Legends]]'' to coincide with the fiftieth anniversary of [[James Bond in film|the James Bond film franchise]].<ref name="Empire">{{cite news|title=Activision Announces 007 Legends|url=https://www.empireonline.com/movies/news/activision-announces-007-legends/|first=Owen|last=Williams|work=Empire|date=19 April 2012|access-date=27 February 2020|archive-date=27 February 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200227092857/https://www.empireonline.com/movies/news/activision-announces-007-legends/|url-status=live}}</ref> The game was described as a "greatest hits compilation",<ref name="Empire"/> retelling six film narratives with an overarching storyline to connect them together. The missions were revealed to be based upon ''[[Goldfinger (film)|Goldfinger]]'', ''[[On Her Majesty's Secret Service (film)|On Her Majesty's Secret Service]]'', ''[[Moonraker (film)|Moonraker]]'', ''[[Licence to Kill]]'' and ''[[Die Another Day]]''. On 9 November 2012, Activision added the last mission to the game, released as a downloadable content, which was based on ''[[Skyfall]]''. The game was released for PlayStation 3, Xbox 360, PC and [[Wii U]] and received mixed reviews from critics. Developer [[Eurocom]] shut down soon after the game's release in December 2012.<ref>{{cite web |author1=IGN |title=007 Legends Video Review |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wCZv0xvCoWg  |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/varchive/youtube/20211212/wCZv0xvCoWg| archive-date=2021-12-12 |url-status=live|website=YouTube |access-date=November 13, 2021 |date=October 16, 2012}}{{cbignore}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.eurogamer.net/articles/2012-12-07-james-bond-developer-eurocom-makes-remaining-staff-redundant-ceases-trading|title=James Bond developer Eurocom makes remaining staff redundant, ceases trading|website=[[Eurogamer]]|date=7 December 2012|access-date=21 December 2012|archive-date=10 December 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121210113236/http://www.eurogamer.net/articles/2012-12-07-james-bond-developer-eurocom-makes-remaining-staff-redundant-ceases-trading|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 4 January 2013, Activision and Steam's online stores removed online availability and pages for ''[[Quantum of Solace (video game)|Quantum of Solace]]'', ''[[James Bond 007: Blood Stone|Blood Stone]]'', and ''[[007 Legends]]'' without explanation or warning,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.gamespot.com/articles/activisions-james-bond-games-disappear-from-steam-and-xbox-360/1100-6402017/3|title=Activision's James Bond games disappear from Steam and Xbox 360|date=4 January 2013|access-date=19 March 2018|archive-date=21 March 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180321063050/https://www.gamespot.com/articles/activisions-james-bond-games-disappear-from-steam-and-xbox-360/1100-6402017/3/|url-status=live}}</ref> only to confirm three days later that the James Bond game license was revoked.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.mi6-hq.com/sections/articles/gaming_activision_game_over.php3|title=Game Over For Activision|date=7 January 2013|access-date=19 March 2018|archive-date=20 March 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180320044009/https://www.mi6-hq.com/sections/articles/gaming_activision_game_over.php3|url-status=live |website=MI6-HQ}}</ref> A month later, Activision themselves declared that they would be backing away from licensed games in a formal statement.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.slashgear.com/activision-is-pulling-away-from-licensed-games-20270334/|title=Activision is pulling away from licensed games|date=20 February 2013|access-date=19 March 2018|archive-date=20 March 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180320105619/https://www.slashgear.com/activision-is-pulling-away-from-licensed-games-20270334/|url-status=live}}</ref>

===Hiatus (2014–2019)===
On 7 January 2014, president and co-founder of [[Telltale Games]], Kevin Bruner had expressed an interest in making a future James Bond game if he were afforded the chance. He stated that "I'm a giant James Bond fan and I'm always frustrated by games that make him a mass murderer." When he was asked which license he would adapt next if money and licensing hurdles were not a factor. "He's a super-spy, and that's a different skillset. The films make him less of a mass murderer, and there's not much killing in the books – more spying and intrigue."<ref>{{cite web |last=Reilly |first=Luke |date=7 January 2014 |url=https://www.ign.com/articles/2014/01/08/telltale-president-keen-to-make-a-james-bond-game |title=Telltale President Keen to Make a James Bond Game |website=[[IGN]] |access-date=7 January 2014 |archive-date=9 January 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140109011208/http://www.ign.com/articles/2014/01/08/telltale-president-keen-to-make-a-james-bond-game |url-status=live }}</ref> A rumour surfaced in June 2017 that Telltale was working on a video game entitled ''007 Solstice''.<ref>{{cite web|date=4 June 2017|url=https://www.mi6-hq.com/sections/articles/gaming-007-solstice-telltale-games-leak?id=04272|title=007 Solstice|publisher=[[Mi6-HQ.com]]|access-date=5 June 2017|archive-date=29 July 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170729123851/https://www.mi6-hq.com/sections/articles/gaming-007-solstice-telltale-games-leak?id=04272|url-status=live}}</ref> However, its status proved unlikely when Telltale filed for bankruptcy and closed down in November 2018.<ref>{{cite magazine|last=Chalk|first=Andy|date=14 November 2018|url=https://www.pcgamer.com/after-some-uncertainty-telltale-games-is-closing-for-good/|title=After some uncertainty, Telltale Games is closing for good|magazine=[[PC Gamer]]|access-date=15 November 2018|archive-date=15 November 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181115064322/https://www.pcgamer.com/after-some-uncertainty-telltale-games-is-closing-for-good/|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 21 January 2016, president of [[Curve Digital]] Dominic Wheatley expressed his interest alongside the company in the series, saying "I'd be very happy to have a James Bond licence. We could do a cracking game around that," adding that these opportunities are overlooked by the bigger firms, since [[Electronic Arts]] and [[Activision]] have their own [[Intellectual property|IP]]s and no longer want to "promote someone else's brand."<ref>{{cite web |last=Dring |first=Christopher |date=21 January 2016 |url=http://www.mcvuk.com/news/read/curve-digital-we-could-make-a-cracking-james-bond-tie-in-game |title=Curve Digital: We could make a cracking James Bond tie-in game |publisher=MCV-UK.com |access-date=21 January 2016 |archive-date=21 February 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160221233727/http://www.mcvuk.com/news/read/curve-digital-we-could-make-a-cracking-james-bond-tie-in-game |url-status=live }}</ref>

In 2016, [[Traveller's Tales]] attempted to pitch a [[Lego video game]] adapting the film series to [[The Lego Group]], who ultimately passed on the project feeling as if the mature tone and explicit depictions of violence and sexuality in the series, did not suit the comparatively younger audience for Lego games.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-12-02 |title=Lego James Bond Pitch Video Leaks Online, Shows Fans What Might Have Been |url=https://www.ign.com/articles/lego-james-bond-pitch-video-leaks-online-shows-fans-what-might-have-been |access-date=2025-04-21 |website=IGN |language=en}}</ref> An internally produced trailer for the game under the codename "Gold", which showed a sizzle reel of recreated moments from the ''Bond'' films, was leaked in December 2024 and corroborated by former TT Games tech director Paul Hughes.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-12-05 |title=A Pitch Video For A Lego James Bond Game Has Leaked |url=https://kotaku.com/lego-james-bond-007-trailer-pitch-leaked-real-tt-games-1851714749 |access-date=2025-04-21 |website=Kotaku |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Blake |first=Vikki |date=2024-12-01 |title=Here's a minute-long tease of the Lego James Bond game we never had |url=https://www.eurogamer.net/heres-a-minute-long-tease-of-the-lego-james-bond-game-we-never-had |access-date=2025-04-21 |website=Eurogamer.net |language=en}}</ref>

===IO Interactive era (2020–present)===
In September 2020, the smartphone game ''Cypher 007'' was released on the [[Apple Arcade]] subscription service and received positive attention from James Bond fans.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Review: Cypher 007 Mobile Game – Chapter 1 |url=https://www.thejamesbonddossier.com/features/review-cypher-007-mobile-game-chapter-1.htm |access-date=2026-04-30 |website=The James Bond Dossier |language=en-US}}</ref>

In November 2020, [[IO Interactive]] announced ''Project 007'', a brand new [[James Bond]] video game, working closely with licensors [[MGM]] and [[Eon Productions]]. IO described the game as a "wholly original Bond story" where "players will step into the shoes of the world's favorite Secret Agent to earn their 00 status in the very first Bond origin story."<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.ign.com/articles/hitman-developer-announces-new-bond-game-project-007 |title=Hitman Developer Announces New Bond Game, Project 007 |first=Joe |last=Skrebels |date=19 November 2020 |website=[[IGN]] |access-date=19 November 2020 |archive-date=19 November 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201119140855/https://www.ign.com/articles/hitman-developer-announces-new-bond-game-project-007 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.eurogamer.net/articles/2020-11-19-hitman-developer-io-reveals-fresh-project |title=Hitman developer IO is making a James Bond game |first=Tom |last=Phillips |date=19 November 2020 |access-date=19 November 2020 |work=[[Eurogamer]] |archive-date=19 November 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201119141134/https://www.eurogamer.net/articles/2020-11-19-hitman-developer-io-reveals-fresh-project |url-status=live}}</ref> The game was officially unveiled as ''[[007 First Light]]'' in June 2025,<ref>{{Cite web |title=007: First Light Is Hitman Dev's James Bond Game, Will Be Revealed This Week |url=https://www.gamespot.com/articles/007-first-light-is-hitman-devs-james-bond-game-will-be-revealed-this-week/1100-6531985/ |access-date=2025-06-02 |website=GameSpot |language=en-US}}</ref> and was released on 26 May 2026 for [[PlayStation 5]], [[Windows]] and [[Xbox Series X/S]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Yin-Poole |first1=Wesley |title=007 First Light Release Date Confirmed During Sony State of Play |url=https://www.ign.com/articles/007-first-light-release-date-confirmed-during-sony-state-of-play |website=IGN |access-date=4 September 2025 |language=en |date=3 September 2025}}</ref> The role of James Bond is portrayed by Irish actor [[Patrick Gibson (actor)|Patrick Gibson]], who provides both voice acting and motion capture performance.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Levy |first1=Giana |last2=Maas |first2=Jennifer |title=Patrick Gibson to Star as James Bond in Video Game ‘007 First Light’; Gameplay Trailer, Release Date Revealed (Gaming News Roundup) |url=https://variety.com/2025/gaming/news/james-bond-game-007-first-light-patrick-gibson-gaming-news-1236506657/ |website=Variety |access-date=1 June 2026 |date=3 September 2025}}</ref>

==Cancelled games==
;''Octopussy'' (1983)
A video game was announced, titled ''Octopussy'', based on the film of the same name. The game was planned for release on the Atari 2600 System, Mattel Intellivision, and compatible systems. Set for release in the summer of 1983, it was cancelled for unknown reasons shortly after it was announced by Parker Brothers.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.mi6-hq.com/sections/games/octopussy_1983.php3?s=games&id=02917|title=Octopussy (1983) Cancelled|website=MI6-HQ|access-date=31 July 2013|archive-date=5 November 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131105050029/http://www.mi6-hq.com/sections/games/octopussy_1983.php3?s=games&id=02917|url-status=live}}</ref>

;''GoldenEye 007'' (1997; 2008)
A racing version of ''[[GoldenEye 007 (1997 video game)|GoldenEye 007]]'' was announced for the [[Virtual Boy]].<ref>{{cite magazine | date = November 1995 | title = Goldeneye Steps Up To NU64 | magazine = Nintendo Power | volume = 78 | page = 112 | url = http://www.planetvb.com/modules/articles/?s004033013 | format = JPEG | access-date = 3 June 2006 | archive-date = 13 September 2012 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20120913063044/http://www.planetvb.com/modules/articles/?s004033013 | url-status = live }}</ref> The game was cancelled in 1996.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.gametrailers.com/video/goldeneye-007-gt-anthology/52623 |title=GoldenEye 007 |date=11 July 2009 |work=GT Anthology |publisher=gametrailers.com |access-date=7 May 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110626033906/http://www.gametrailers.com/video/goldeneye-007-gt-anthology/52623 |archive-date=26 June 2011 |df=dmy-all }}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.planetvb.com/modules/articles/?w009 | title=Games – Unreleased – GoldenEye | publisher=Planet Virtual Boy | access-date=8 January 2007 | archive-date=13 September 2012 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120913062900/http://www.planetvb.com/modules/articles/?w009 | url-status=live }}</ref>

A remastered version of the [[Nintendo 64]] game ''GoldenEye 007'' by [[Rare (company)|Rare]] was scheduled for release on [[Xbox 360]]'s [[Xbox Live Arcade|Live Arcade]] on 27 February 2008, but [[Microsoft]] (who acquired Rare and their intellectual properties in 2002) couldn't get the publishing rights from the intellectual property owners, [[Danjaq, LLC]], resulting in the cancelation of the project, despite being nearly completed.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.videogamer.com/news/rare-xbla-goldeneye-locked-in-no-mans-land|title=Rare: XBLA GoldenEye 'locked in no man's land'|website=VideoGamer.com|date=6 August 2008|language=en|access-date=2019-09-20|archive-date=3 February 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210203233226/https://www.videogamer.com/news/rare-xbla-goldeneye-locked-in-no-mans-land|url-status=live}}</ref> It was rumored that [[Nintendo]] (the publisher of the original title) or [[Activision]] (who had exclusive rights to publish video games based on the James Bond franchise at the time) may have been involved in the project's cancellation, but no sources confirm the rumor. Despite this, in January 2021, a near-final build of the game was leaked online from an unknown source, which led to many players playing the ROM via emulation.<ref>{{Cite web|url = https://www.videogameschronicle.com/news/goldeneyes-xbox-remaster-has-leaked-online-and-its-fully-playable-on-pc/|title = GoldenEye's Xbox remaster has leaked online – and it's fully playable on PC|date = 3 February 2021|access-date = 19 March 2021|archive-date = 3 March 2021|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20210303212055/https://www.videogameschronicle.com/news/goldeneyes-xbox-remaster-has-leaked-online-and-its-fully-playable-on-pc/|url-status = live}}</ref>

;''Tomorrow Never Dies: The Mission Continues'' (1998)
The original VHS release of ''[[Tomorrow Never Dies]]'' featured a brief trailer with [[Desmond Llewelyn]] which highlighted a game that would "start where the film ends".<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=aDCEvZQxvHw&ab_channel=VTRVCR |archive-date=16 September 2022 |title=Tomorrow Never Dies Video Game |publisher=YouTube |date=21 December 2007 |access-date=22 May 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220916034538/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=aDCEvZQxvHw&ab_channel=VTRVCR }}</ref> Footage shows Bond skiing, scuba diving and driving in third person and on a [[First-person shooter|first-person]] shooting mission.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.ign.com/games/007-tomorrow-never-dies/images |title=007: Tomorrow Never Dies Images|publisher=IGN |access-date=13 November 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120331192159/http://media.psx.ign.com/media/002/002310/imgs_7.html |archive-date=31 March 2012 |df=dmy-all }}</ref> The game was to come out on [[PlayStation (console)|PlayStation]] and PC in the fall of 1998 and was being made by [[MGM Interactive]], not [[EA]]; EA was not involved in Bond until November of that year.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.ign.com/articles/1998/11/21/ea-and-mgm-bond |title=EA and MGM Bond |work=IGN |date=21 November 1998 |access-date=22 May 2012 |archive-date=13 August 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190813181340/https://www.ign.com/articles/1998/11/21/ea-and-mgm-bond |url-status=live }}</ref> Because MGM's motion picture division had licensed exclusive James Bond console rights to Nintendo (for ''GoldenEye 007'' for the Nintendo 64), MGM had to buy some of their rights back from Nintendo in order to make the game.<ref>{{cite magazine |title=Gaming Gossip |magazine=[[Electronic Gaming Monthly]]|issue=97 |publisher=[[Ziff Davis]] |date=August 1997|page=32}}</ref>

A ''[[Tomorrow Never Dies (video game)|Tomorrow Never Dies]]'' game was released on 16 November 1999, distributed by EA, but with notable differences from the 1998 attempt. The game was a [[third-person shooter]] with no scuba diving level. The story follows the plot of the film, not the continuation that had been planned. A level in the game sees Bond skiing down a mountain and killing a Japanese terrorist named Sotoshi Isagura (who had featured very briefly in the film), while in another stage Bond has a driving mission in Switzerland. These were not from the original film so may have survived from the 'continuation' story.

;''The World Is Not Enough'' (2000)
A game based on the 1999 film ''The World Is Not Enough'' film and using the ''[[Quake III Arena]]'' engine for the [[Personal computer|PC]] and [[PlayStation 2]] was cancelled in favour of ''[[James Bond 007: Agent Under Fire|Agent Under Fire]]''.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ign.com/articles/2001/04/27/the-world-is-not-enough-6|title=The World Is Not Enough|publisher=IGN|date=27 April 2001|access-date=13 November 2021|archive-date=13 November 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211113182048/https://www.ign.com/articles/2001/04/27/the-world-is-not-enough-6|url-status=live}}</ref> Electronic Arts thought, by 2001, that too much time had passed since the release of the film, and that fans would be no longer interested in the product as talks of the succeeding film in the series, ''[[Die Another Day]]'', were taking place.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.mi6-hq.com/sections/articles/gaming_twine_pc.php3 |title=The World Is Not Enough on PC and PS2 |publisher=MI6-HQ.com |date=6 January 2007 |access-date=13 September 2014 |archive-date=13 September 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140913132217/http://www.mi6-hq.com/sections/articles/gaming_twine_pc.php3 |url-status=live }}</ref>

;''007 Racing'' sequel (2001)
A PlayStation 2 sequel to ''[[007 Racing]]'' was rumoured to be in development.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.ign.com/articles/2000/12/12/bond-races-to-playstation-2-again |title=Bond Races to PlayStation 2 Again |publisher=IGN |date=11 December 2000 |access-date=November 13, 2021 |archive-date=13 November 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211113182048/https://www.ign.com/articles/2000/12/12/bond-races-to-playstation-2-again |url-status=live }}</ref>

;''Bond6'' (2005)
EA Games began conceptual work on the game in 2003, under the working title of ''Bond6''. The game was originally meant to be released in 2005, set to star [[Pierce Brosnan]] as [[James Bond (character)|James Bond]]. A video game adaptation of ''[[From Russia with Love (video game)|From Russia with Love]]'' began development when Brosnan announced that he was stepping down from the role, which ended plans for ''Bond6''. The opening level planned for the former was retooled for the latter, and CGI work intended for the game was reused in television commercials for ''GoldenEye: Rogue Agent''.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.mi6-hq.com/sections/articles/gaming_frwl_firstnews.php3?t=frwlgame&s=frwlgame&id=0680|title=James Bond 007: "From Russia With Love" by EA Games|website=MI6-HQ.COM|access-date=13 November 2021|archive-date=23 September 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210923111149/https://www.mi6-hq.com/sections/articles/gaming_frwl_firstnews.php3?t=frwlgame&s=frwlgame&id=0680|url-status=live}}</ref>

;''Casino Royale'' (2006)
A game was in development based on [[Casino Royale (2006 film)|the film of the same name]]. [[Daniel Craig]], in character as Bond, was going to give his voice and likeness to the video game. It was set to release on the PlayStation 3 and Xbox 360 platforms. The game was 15% developed when the project was cancelled, as Electronic Arts would not finish it by the film's release in November 2006. Later, unfinished development screenshots from the Venice level were uncovered.<ref name="Fritz"/><ref name="EA CR"/><ref name="LostGame"/> Activision's debut in the series, ''[[Quantum of Solace (video game)|Quantum of Solace]]'', combines the storylines of ''Casino Royale'' and ''Quantum of Solace''.

;''Blood Stone'' sequel (2011)
In December 2010, some screenshots and a video were leaked online that depicted a new James Bond game, which shared similar gameplay to its predecessor, ''Blood Stone''. Reportedly, the project had been in development by [[Raven Software]], but was postponed six months prior to the leak, at which point the game was believed to be back in development. However, the game was ultimately cancelled due to ''Blood Stone's'' poor sales.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.mi6-hq.com/sections/articles/gaming_activision_raven_first_look.php3 |title=First Look At Next 007 Game |publisher=MI6-HQ.com |date=7 December 2010 |access-date=12 September 2016 |archive-date=13 April 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160413135723/https://www.mi6-hq.com///sections/articles/gaming_activision_raven_first_look.php3 |url-status=live }}</ref>

;''Skyfall'' (2012)
In January 2012, it was announced that a video game based on ''[[Skyfall]]'' would be released by Activision.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://gamerant.com/james-bond-skyfall-video-game-curt-123548/|title=James Bond 'Skyfall' Game In The Works|publisher=GameRant|date=3 January 2012|access-date=12 September 2016|archive-date=23 September 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160923142114/https://gamerant.com/james-bond-skyfall-video-game-curt-123548/|url-status=live}}</ref> Ultimately, a downloadable level based on ''Skyfall'' was released for Activision's ''[[007 Legends]]'', although a full game was not released.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.gamespot.com/articles/skyfall-mission-in-007-legends-launches-first-for-ps3/1100-6398323/|title=Skyfall mission in 007 Legends launches first for PS3|website=GameSpot|date=16 October 2012|access-date=12 September 2016|archive-date=14 March 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150314052135/http://www.gamespot.com/articles/skyfall-mission-in-007-legends-launches-first-for-ps3/1100-6398323/|url-status=live}}</ref>

;''Lego James Bond'' 
In 2005 [[TT Games]] produced a test animation as part of a pitch for a [[Lego]] ''James Bond'' video game. While the project was initially approved by Lego, Activision and the [[Albert R. Broccoli|Broccoli family]], the idea was abandoned shortly after the release of ''[[Casino Royale (2006 film)|Casino Royale]]'' a year later, as the films darker and more violent tone was considered unsuitable for Lego's family-friendly demographic.<ref>{{cite video |title=LEGO Games that nearly got made (the last one would …) |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fIgu-DKTD54 |publisher=GameHut |website=YouTube |date=April 17, 2017}}</ref>

In 2016, TT Games pitched another ''James Bond'' themed entry in their long running line of Lego games, which would adapt the events of multiple films. The pitch was rejected for largely the same reasons. A trailer for the game was later leaked in 2024.<ref>{{cite web | last=Blake | first=Vikki | title=Here's a minute-long tease of the Lego James Bond game we never had | website=Eurogamer.net | date=December 1, 2024 | url=https://www.eurogamer.net/heres-a-minute-long-tease-of-the-lego-james-bond-game-we-never-had | access-date=December 1, 2024}}</ref>

==Other games==

===Mobile and smartphone games===
Since 2002, games featuring the Bond character and the ''007'' trademark have been published and distributed on mobile phones. The first two are based on action sequences from ''[[Die Another Day]]'', one of them is titled ''Hover Chase'' and the other is ''Ice Racer''. Both were published by [[Vodafone]].

With the official reboot of the film franchise in 2006, [[Sony Online Entertainment]] released a side-scroll action game based on ''[[Casino Royale (2006 film)|Casino Royale]]'' developed by [[Glu Mobile]], following a storyline inspired by the film. Similarly, an identical tie-in based on ''[[Quantum of Solace (film)|Quantum of Solace]]'' was released in 2008 by the same team. The same year, Sony Online Entertainment Los Angeles developed and published an arcade [[fighting game]] to coincide with the aforementioned film, entitled ''Top Agent''.

In 2014, it was reported that Glu Mobile was working on another mobile game bearing the James Bond license.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.marketwatch.com/story/glu-to-create-james-bond-game-with-eon-productions-and-mgm-interactive-2014-04-08?reflink=MW_news_stmp|title=Glu to Create James Bond Game with EON Productions and MGM Interactive|publisher=MarketWatch|date=8 April 2014|access-date=12 April 2014|archive-date=13 April 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140413130751/http://www.marketwatch.com/story/glu-to-create-james-bond-game-with-eon-productions-and-mgm-interactive-2014-04-08?reflink=MW_news_stmp|url-status=live}}</ref> A year later, its title was revealed as ''World of Espionage'',<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.mi6-hq.com/sections/articles/gaming-next-bond-game-2015?t&s&id=03909|title=The Next Bond Game by Glu Mobile|publisher=MI6-HQ.com|date=2 June 2015|access-date=2 June 2015|archive-date=30 June 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150630235858/https://www.mi6-hq.com/sections/articles/gaming-next-bond-game-2015?t&s&id=03909|url-status=live}}</ref> a [[Point-and-click Adventure|point-and-click]] game retelling several previous storylines from the film series, debuting an [[early access]] mode in July 2015 and releasing a full version of the game in November later that year.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.mi6-hq.com/sections/articles/gaming-jbwoe-james-bond-world-of-espionage-launched?t=&s=&id=03931|title=James Bond: World of Espionage|publisher=MI6-HQ.com|date=18 July 2015|access-date=19 July 2015|archive-date=22 July 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150722070537/https://www.mi6-hq.com/sections/articles/gaming-jbwoe-james-bond-world-of-espionage-launched?t=&s=&id=03931|url-status=live}}</ref> The game, after being universally panned for its uninspired content, was removed from the online mobile stores in December 2016 and Glu Mobile pulled the plug on the title.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.mi6-hq.com/sections/articles/gaming-glu-mobile-cancel-james-bond-world-of-espionage?id=04193|title=Game Over for Glu Mobile|publisher=MI6-HQ.com|date=2 December 2016|access-date=4 December 2016|archive-date=20 December 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161220061847/https://www.mi6-hq.com/sections/articles/gaming-glu-mobile-cancel-james-bond-world-of-espionage?id=04193|url-status=live}}</ref>

===Fanmade remakes===
{{Further|GoldenEye: Source}}

With the popularity laid by ''[[GoldenEye 007 (1997 video game)|GoldenEye 007]]'' in 1997 on the Nintendo 64, fans of the video game have made many attempts to remake or recreate the title with updated makeovers on current engines over time. But, only one project succeeded. Entitled ''[[GoldenEye: Source]]'', the game entered development in 2005 and officially saw its international release in 2010, five years after being in [[Software release life cycle#Beta|beta mode]] hosted by the [[Source (engine)|Source]] engine. It is a [[Mod (computer gaming)#Total conversion|total conversion mod]] based on the multiplayer mode from the aforementioned title.

A different team initiated similar attempts in 2013 to port the multiplayer mode from ''[[James Bond 007: Nightfire|Nightfire]]'' (2002) to the Source engine, hoping to release it on [[Steam (service)|Steam]] under the title ''Nightfire: Source''. The project, as of today, remains in development.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://community.nightfiresource.com/|title=Nightfire: Source Community|access-date=27 October 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131029194459/http://community.nightfiresource.com/|archive-date=29 October 2013|df=dmy-all}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://pcgmedia.com/nightfire-being-remade-in-source-engine/ |title='Nightfire' being remade in Source Engine |publisher=PCGMedia |date=27 July 2013 |access-date=27 October 2013 |archive-date=29 October 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131029184416/http://pcgmedia.com/nightfire-being-remade-in-source-engine/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

To commemorate the video game's 25th anniversary, another project based on ''GoldenEye 007'' entered development in 2017 on [[Unreal Engine 4]], with the aim of releasing it sometime in August 2022, based on the title's [[Single-player video game|single-player]] campaign.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://kotaku.com/one-goldeneye-fan-wants-to-recreate-the-entire-thing-in-1829665819|title=One GoldenEye Fan Wants To Recreate The Entire Game In Unreal|date=10 October 2018|publisher=Kotaku|access-date=21 October 2018|archive-date=11 October 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181011000723/https://kotaku.com/one-goldeneye-fan-wants-to-recreate-the-entire-thing-in-1829665819|url-status=live}}</ref> However, in August 2020, the team received a [[cease and desist]] letter from [[Danjaq]], forbidding the remake and stripping its use of any licensed asset related to the property, including [[James Bond (film character)|James Bond]] and related characters.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.eurogamer.net/articles/2020-08-11-after-years-of-development-the-goldeneye-25-fan-remake-just-got-lawyered|title=After years of development, the GoldenEye 25 fan remake just got lawyered|publisher=Eurogamer|date=11 August 2020|access-date=12 August 2020|archive-date=12 August 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200812203511/https://www.eurogamer.net/articles/2020-08-11-after-years-of-development-the-goldeneye-25-fan-remake-just-got-lawyered|url-status=live}}</ref> The project was reborn as ''Spies Don't Die'' – an original experience "inspired by 90s first-person shooters".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://twitter.com/spiesdontdie|title='Spies Don't Die' on Twitter|publisher=Twitter|date=10 August 2020|access-date=12 August 2020|archive-date=12 August 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200812153035/https://twitter.com/spiesdontdie|url-status=live}}</ref>

===Appearance in other media===
Downloadable content featuring a pack of cars used in the James Bond films is available in ''[[Forza Horizon 4]]'', officially branded and licensed by Danjaq, LLC.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.eurogamer.net/articles/2018-09-13-forza-horizon-4-gets-james-bond-dlc|title=Forza Horizon 4 is getting James Bond DLC|website=[[Eurogamer]]|date=13 September 2018|access-date=19 September 2018|archive-date=19 September 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180919171929/https://www.eurogamer.net/articles/2018-09-13-forza-horizon-4-gets-james-bond-dlc|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.mi6-hq.com/sections/articles/gaming-forza-4-horizon-best-of-bond-cars?id=04421|title=Best of Bond Cars|website=MI6-HQ |date=17 September 2018|access-date=19 September 2018|archive-date=19 September 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180919211512/https://www.mi6-hq.com/sections/articles/gaming-forza-4-horizon-best-of-bond-cars?id=04421|url-status=live}}</ref>

James Bond is parodied in ''[[Broforce]]'' as a playable character, Double Bro Seven, whose name is a pun on Bond's code number [[007]], with his appearance being based on either [[Sean Connery]], [[George Lazenby]] or [[Pierce Brosnan]]. Just like the actual Bond, he wears a tuxedo and uses a pistol. Unlike other characters in the game, he has a variety of special skills, including a martini, needed for a trophy called "[[Shaken, not stirred]]", which is a joke on a famous Bond catchphrase.

The Proximity Mine item from ''[[GoldenEye 007 (1997 video game)|GoldenEye 007]]'' is present in [[Nintendo]]'s ''[[Super Smash Bros.]]'' series, where it is renamed the Motion-Sensor Bomb. It was first introduced to the series in [[Super Smash Bros. (video game)|the first game]] and made a return in all non-Japanese versions of ''[[Super Smash Bros. Melee]]''. The Japanese version of ''Super Smash Bros. Melee'' instead has the item's design from ''[[Perfect Dark]]'', the spiritual successor to ''GoldenEye 007''. Additionally, references to ''GoldenEye 007'' is minimized, with the origin of the Motion-Sensor Bomb listed as "TOP SECRET" in the Western releases. From ''[[Super Smash Bros. Brawl]]'' onward, the Motion Sensor-Bomb was redesigned completely with any resemblance to its original design gone and is instead treated as an original item from the ''Super Smash Bros.'' series.
